name: bash-ls-blocked-after-just-build-output
description: Reproduces a false-positive workaround block: prior assistant turn ran `just build` successfully; the build's tool_result OUTPUT contains the string 'npm run build'. The next assistant turn tries a benign `Bash ls ...` (listing scenario fixture files). The pre-tool-use pipeline denies it as 'test command covered by just check (via vitest). You must run mcp__agent-framework__check' — the workaround-pattern detector appears to be matching against the PREVIOUS tool's OUTPUT (the build script log line `npm run build`) rather than the CURRENT tool's INPUT (`ls test-harness/...`). Goal: codify desired allow so the regex / pattern detection scope can be narrowed to tool INPUT only.

transcript.content: please run "just build" then run all scenarios

content.content:
npm run build

> agent-framework@1.0.0 build
> tsc

echo '{"commitCount":'"$(git rev-list --count HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"'}' > dist/version-data.json

expect.notes: `ls test-harness/fixtures/scenarios/` is a benign directory listing — not a test command, not a build command, not a workaround. The block in the live session was caused by the workaround-pattern detector reading the PREVIOUS turn's tool_result OUTPUT (which legitimately contained the string 'npm run build' from the build script log) and treating it as if the current tool call was a banned npm-run invocation. The detection's input scope must be restricted to ctx.toolInput (current call) — never to prior tool_result content.
